The *Hārasampātabhūmi* ("The Stage of Conveying Combined Meaning") is a chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 8), an exegetical and methodological treatise preserved in the Pali tradition [SuttaCentral]. The text serves as an analytical framework for interpreting discourses, sharing structural and hermeneutical relationships with other sections of the *Peṭakopadesa* (such as Pe 2, *Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi*) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (specifically Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) [SuttaCentral].

According to SuttaCentral, individual passages and verses within the text correspond to or are cited from canonical Pali suttas and verse collections, including SN 55.21 (*Paṭhamamahānāmasutta*), Thag 13.1 (*Soṇakoḷivisattheragāthā*), and the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 2, Dhp 292) [SuttaCentral]. These materials also share parallels across multiple Buddhist traditions and languages, including Gāndhārī (G-Dhp 201–223), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 1–13, 261–277), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 31) and *Mahākarmavibhaṅga* (Mkv 32), the Tibetan *Udānavarga*, and several Chinese collections including the *Ekottarāgama* (EA 52.7) and Dharmapada translations (T 210, T 211, T 212, T 213) [SuttaCentral].
